description: ODC (E/D coverage): the LIFECYCLE of a user exception AFTER birth. The ODC lane already proved creating (switch-exception-handler creates the WfCovUiFailure, the UI flow, the On Exception and the IExceptionHandlerNode that handles it); what it never proved was touching what already existed. That is why the base of this job IS that job: everything that is edited, renamed, repointed and deleted here WAS BORN in another job, and none of it is recreated here. The four operations are, in order: (1) RENAME the inherited element -- the exception becomes WfLcUiFailure and the inherited handler keeps handling it without being touched, because the consumers stay connected by KEY, and the flow becomes WfLcErrorFlow, which leaves the message of the inherited IMessageNode citing the old name (a literal does not follow a rename: I fix it by hand, in the job itself); (2) EDIT the inherited element -- IExceptionHandlerNode.Exception is a writable property, so swapping the exception that a handler handles is a set on a node that already existed, not a new handler, and the node keeps the key, the AbortTransaction and the LogError it had; (3) REPOINT -- the two IRaiseExceptionNode that raise the old exception move to the new one with a single replace (the same ReplaceReferences of the Studio), and the ExceptionMessage of each one, being a literal, stays as it was; (4) DELETE -- with the handler already on another exception and the raises already repointed, the old one is left with zero consumers and the delete passes WITHOUT force. The two raisers are created here on purpose and are the only new thing in logic: the inherited job had nobody raising the exception, and without consumers there is nothing to repoint nor anything to 'handle before deleting'. The numbers that follow are the usages of the inherited exception: 1 (only the handler) -> 3 (handler + two raises) -> 2 (the handler left in the edit) -> 0 (the replace took the raises) -> deleted.

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio gives an error); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops._why: (1) INHERITED STARTING POINT, read before any write: the handler, the On Exception that contains it and the exception that it handles came from job:switch-exception-handler. This job creates none of the three
(1) the inherited exception has exactly ONE real consumer, the inherited IExceptionHandlerNode

ops.name: WfLcUiFailure
ops._why: (2) RENAME THE INHERITED ELEMENT. The rename returns consumers=1: the handler is not touched and keeps handling the SAME exception, because what links is the key and not the text of the name
(2) read back the inherited handler: Exception already says WfLcUiFailure without a single set on it

ops.name: WfLcErrorFlow
ops._why: (2b) the second rename of an inherited element exists to show the LIMIT of the rename, not only what it can do: the UI flow changes name and the On Exception stays its child

(2b) and here is the limit: the Message of the inherited IMessageNode STILL says 'WfCovErrorFlow'. Text literals never follow a rename (AGENTS.md, section 2, 'Renomear'); whoever trusts the rename delivers the old name showing to the user. Access note: the inherited node cannot be reached by '/ShowError', even though the previous job created it with that name -- the IMessageNode is one more of the types that DISCARD the name of the create (like If, Assign, Switch and ForEach), so the path is by type, '/#IMessageNode'
(2b) HAND fix of the literal, which is the part the platform does for nobody
(2b) and the text is now the new one

ops.name: WfLc_Notice_Submit
ops._why: (3) the raisers are the ONLY new logic of the job, and they exist out of necessity: the inherited job created the exception and the handler, but nobody raised it. Without consumers there is nothing to repoint in (5) nor anything to 'handle before' in (6)

ops.value: Ciclo de vida: submete um aviso e levanta a excecao herdada quando o titulo vem vazio

ops.name: RaiseSubmitFailure
ops._why: the name here is DISCARDED, as in the ISwitchNode of the inherited job: an IRaiseExceptionNode keeps no Name and what appears in the flow (DisplayName) is the NAME OF THE EXCEPTION it raises -- so the get of (5) is the visual proof of the replace: the same node now shows WfLcSubmitFailed without anyone writing anything to it
raises the INHERITED exception, already with the name that the rename gave it
on purpose a message that does NOT cite the name of the exception: it is a literal, and the replace of (5) would not rewrite it
the IRaiseExceptionNode is TERMINAL for the layout, like the End: it takes no outgoing connector

ops.name: WfLc_Notice_Withdraw
ops._why: (3) the second raiser: more than one is needed for the replace to prove that it repoints ALL of them and not just the first one it finds

ops.value: Ciclo de vida: retira um aviso e levanta a mesma excecao herdada quando ele ja nao e rascunho
"Only a draft notice can be withdrawn"

ops._why: (3) three real consumers: the inherited IExceptionHandlerNode and the two IRaiseExceptionNode created now

ops.name: WfLcSubmitFailed
ops._why: (4) the specific exception that is going to replace the inherited, generic one: it is the ONLY top-level object that this job creates of its own accord. No set after it: in ODC an IUserException has no writable Description (the writable ones are CreatedBy, LastModifiedBy, LastModifiedDate and Name), so the name is all it carries

(4) THE EDIT THAT GIVES THE JOB ITS NAME: swapping the exception handled by a handler is a set on a property of a node that ALREADY EXISTED. The IExceptionHandlerNode is neither deleted nor recreated; it keeps the key, the position in the diagram, the connector to the ShowError and the AbortTransaction/LogError that the previous job gave it
(4) read back: Exception is WfLcSubmitFailed, AbortTransaction and LogError are still the inherited ones

ops.name: HandleSubmitFailed
ops._why: (4) the name of the inherited node also lies after the edit ('HandleAll' no longer handles everything); node names follow the style of the inherited job and do not take the Wf prefix, which is for top-level objects
(4) the proof that this was an EDIT and not a recreation is in the key: Key/ObjectKey and Target are the SAME as in the first get of this job, with another Exception and another Name
(4) the whole inherited On Exception after the edits: the same handler (with new name and exception) connected to the same ShowError and the same End
(4) the old one fell from 3 to 2: the handler left, the two raises remain
(4) and the new one already has 1: the inherited handler

(5) REPOINT WHO RAISES IT: a single replace moves the TWO IRaiseExceptionNode to the new exception. It is not text search-and-replace and each node keeps its key; the ExceptionMessage, being a literal, is not touched
(5) it has to end at zero
(5) tres: o handler herdado e os dois raise
(5) the repointed node: Exception is WfLcSubmitFailed and the literal message is the same as ever

(6) DELETE WITH THE CONSUMERS HANDLED BEFORE: one of them left by edit (the handler) and two by replace (the raises); with zero consumers the delete passes WITHOUT force and returns brokenConsumers=0. The refusal of this same operation with consumers is in tests/jobs-odc/delete-logic-in-use.json

ops._why: (6) vazio: a excecao deixou de existir

ops.name: WfCovUiFailure
ops._why: (6) also empty, but for another reason: this name died in the rename of (2), not in the delete

ops.name: WfLcSubmitFailed
ops._why: (6) the one that remains
